questions.problem:
Consider the function $L:{R}^{2\times 3}\to R$ defined by $L(A)={y}^{T}Ax$ where 

$$
x=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 10 \\ 20\end{aligned}],\,y=[\begin{aligned}7 \\ 8\end{aligned}].
$$

What is ${∇}_{A}L$ at 
$A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 0 \\ 4 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]?$
questions.worked_solution:
The gradient of $L$ with respect to $A$ is a matrix of the same shape as $A$, with $(i,j)$th entry given by

$$
\frac{∂L}{∂{a}_{ij}},
$$

the partial derivative of $L$ with respect to the $(i,j)$th entry of $A.$

Writing out $L$ in component-wise notation as 

$$
L={\sum }_{i=1}^{2}{\sum }_{j=1}^{3}{a}_{ij}{y}_{i}{x}_{j},
$$

we have

$$
\frac{∂L}{∂{a}_{ij}}={y}_{i}{x}_{j}.
$$

Thus, ${∇}_{A}L=y\cdot {x}^{T}.$

Evaluating at the given values $x=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 10 \\ 20\end{aligned}]$ and $y=[\begin{aligned}7 \\ 8\end{aligned}],$ we get

$$
{∇}_{A}L=[\begin{aligned}7 \\ 8\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}0 & 10 & 20\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 & 70 & 140 \\ 0 & 80 & 160\end{aligned}].
$$

Consider the function $L:{R}^{2\times 2}\to R$ defined by $L(A)=2({y}^{T}Ax)$ where 

$$
x=[\begin{aligned}9 \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,y=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1\end{aligned}].
$$

What is ${∇}_{A}L$ at 
$A=[\begin{aligned}10 & 10 \\ -5 & -5\end{aligned}]?$
questions.worked_solution:
The gradient of $L$ with respect to $A$ is a matrix of the same shape as $A$, with $(i,j)$th entry given by

$$
\frac{∂L}{∂{a}_{ij}},
$$

the partial derivative of $L$ with respect to the $(i,j)$th entry of $A.$

Writing out $L$ in component-wise notation as 

$$
L={\sum }_{i=1}^{2}{\sum }_{j=1}^{2}{a}_{ij}{y}_{i}{x}_{j},
$$

we have

$$
\frac{∂L}{∂{a}_{ij}}={y}_{i}{x}_{j}.
$$

Thus, ${∇}_{A}L=2(y\cdot {x}^{T}).$

Evaluating at the given values $x=[\begin{aligned}9 \\ 0\end{aligned}]$ and $y=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1\end{aligned}],$ we get

$$
{∇}_{A}L=2([\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}9 & 0\end{aligned}])=2([\begin{aligned}9 & 0 \\ -9 & 0\end{aligned}])=[\begin{aligned}18 & 0 \\ -18 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$

questions.problem:
Consider the function $L:{R}^{3\times 2}\to R$ defined by $L(A)=3({y}^{T}Ax)$ where 

$$
x=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 3\end{aligned}],\,y=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -1 \\ 4\end{aligned}].
$$

What is ${∇}_{A}L$ at 
$A=[\begin{aligned}-2 & 3 \\ 5 & 1 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}]?$
questions.worked_solution:
The gradient of $L$ with respect to $A$ is a matrix of the same shape as $A$, with $(i,j)$th entry given by

$$
\frac{∂L}{∂{a}_{ij}},
$$

the partial derivative of $L$ with respect to the $(i,j)$th entry of $A.$

Writing out $L$ in component-wise notation as 

$$
L={\sum }_{i=1}^{3}{\sum }_{j=1}^{2}3{a}_{ij}{y}_{i}{x}_{j},
$$

we have

$$
\frac{∂L}{∂{a}_{ij}}=3{y}_{i}{x}_{j}.
$$

Thus, ${∇}_{A}L=3(y\cdot {x}^{T}).$

Evaluating at the given values $x=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 3\end{aligned}]$ and $y=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -1 \\ 4\end{aligned}],$ we get

$$
{∇}_{A}L=3([\begin{aligned}0 \\ -1 \\ 4\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}3 & 3\end{aligned}])=3([\begin{aligned}0 & 0 \\ -3 & -3 \\ 12 & 12\end{aligned}])=[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 \\ -9 & -9 \\ 36 & 36\end{aligned}].
$$

questions.problem:
Consider the function $L:{R}^{2\times 2}\to R$ defined by $L(A)=\frac{1}{2}(Ax-b)^{T}(Ax-b),$ where $$ x=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 3\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 4\end{aligned}]. $$ What is ${∇}_{A}L$ at $A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 2 & -1\end{aligned}]?$
${∇}_{A}=\,\,$ {{field-1}} $9$
$-6$ {{field-2}}
questions.worked_solution:
The gradient of $L$ with respect to $A$ is a matrix of the same shape as $A$, with $(i,j)$th entry given by

$$
\frac{∂L}{∂{a}_{ij}},
$$

the partial derivative of $L$ with respect to the $(i,j)$th entry of $A.$

We can compute $\frac{∂L}{∂{a}_{ij}}$ by applying the chain rule.

Let $y=Ax-b\in {R}^{2}.$ Then, $L(A)=\frac{1}{2}{y}^{T}y$ and

$$
\frac{∂L}{∂{a}_{ij}}={\sum }_{k=1}^{2}\frac{∂L}{∂{y}_{k}}\cdot \frac{∂{y}_{k}}{∂{a}_{ij}}
$$

Now, since 

$$
{∇}_{y}L={∇}_{y}(\frac{1}{2}{y}^{T}y)=y,
$$

we have that

$$
\frac{∂L}{∂{y}_{k}}={y}_{k}.
$$

Writing out $y=Ax-b$ in component-wise notation as 

$$
{y}_{i}={\sum }_{j=1}^{2}{a}_{ij}{x}_{j}-{b}_{i},
$$

we have 

- $\frac{∂{y}_{k}}{∂{a}_{ij}}={x}_{j}$ if $i=k$, and

- $\frac{∂{y}_{k}}{∂{a}_{ij}}=0$ if $i\ne k.$

This means that 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂L}{∂{a}_{ij}} & ={\sum }_{k=1}^{2}\frac{∂L}{∂{y}_{k}}\cdot \frac{∂{y}_{k}}{∂{a}_{ij}} \\  & =\frac{∂L}{∂{y}_{i}}\cdot \frac{∂{y}_{i}}{∂{a}_{ij}} \\  & ={y}_{i}\cdot \frac{∂{y}_{i}}{∂{a}_{ij}} \\  & ={y}_{i}{x}_{j}.\end{aligned}
$$

The $(i,j)$th entry of ${∇}_{A}L$ is the $i$th entry of $y$ multiplied by the $j$th entry of $x$, so

$$
{∇}_{A}L=y\cdot {x}^{T}.
$$

Finally, evaluating ${∇}_{A}L$ at $A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 2 & -1\end{aligned}],$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{∇}_{A}L & =y\cdot {x}^{T} \\  & =(Ax-b)\cdot {x}^{T} \\  & =([\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 2 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 \\ 3\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 4\end{aligned}])\cdot [\begin{aligned}2 & 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =([\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 4\end{aligned}])\cdot [\begin{aligned}2 & 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -3\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}2 & 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}6 & 9 \\ -6 & -9\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Consider the function $L:{R}^{2\times 2}\to R$ defined by $L(A)=(4Ax-5b)^{T}(4Ax-5b),$ where $$ x=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 4\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 3\end{aligned}]. $$ What is ${∇}_{A}L$ at $A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}]?$
${∇}_{A}=\,\,$ {{field-1}} $832$
$0$ {{field-2}}
questions.worked_solution:
The gradient of $L$ with respect to $A$ is a matrix of the same shape as $A$, with $(i,j)$th entry given by

$$
\frac{∂L}{∂{a}_{ij}},
$$

the partial derivative of $L$ with respect to the $(i,j)$th entry of $A.$

We can compute $\frac{∂L}{∂{a}_{ij}}$ by applying the chain rule.

Let $y=4Ax-5b\in {R}^{2}.$ Then, $L(A)={y}^{T}y$ and

$$
\frac{∂L}{∂{a}_{ij}}={\sum }_{k=1}^{2}\frac{∂L}{∂{y}_{k}}\cdot \frac{∂{y}_{k}}{∂{a}_{ij}}
$$

Now, since 

$$
{∇}_{y}L={∇}_{y}({y}^{T}y)=2y,
$$

we have that

$$
\frac{∂L}{∂{y}_{k}}=2{y}_{k}.
$$

Writing out $y=4Ax-5b$ in component-wise notation as 

$$
{y}_{i}=4{\sum }_{j=1}^{2}{a}_{ij}{x}_{j}-5{b}_{i},
$$

we have 

- $\frac{∂{y}_{k}}{∂{a}_{ij}}=4{x}_{j}$ if $i=k$, and

- $\frac{∂{y}_{k}}{∂{a}_{ij}}=0$ if $i\ne k.$

This means that 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂L}{∂{a}_{ij}} & ={\sum }_{k=1}^{2}\frac{∂L}{∂{y}_{k}}\cdot \frac{∂{y}_{k}}{∂{a}_{ij}} \\  & =\frac{∂L}{∂{y}_{i}}\cdot \frac{∂{y}_{i}}{∂{a}_{ij}} \\  & =2{y}_{i}\cdot \frac{∂{y}_{i}}{∂{a}_{ij}} \\  & =2{y}_{i}\cdot 4{x}_{j} \\  & =8{y}_{i}{x}_{j}.\end{aligned}
$$

The $(i,j)$th entry of ${∇}_{A}L$ is $8$ times the $i$th entry of $y$ multiplied by the $j$th entry of $x$, so

$$
{∇}_{A}L=8y\cdot {x}^{T}.
$$

Finally, evaluating ${∇}_{A}L$ at $A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}],$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{∇}_{A}L & =8y\cdot {x}^{T} \\  & =8(4Ax-5b)\cdot {x}^{T} \\  & =8(4[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ 4\end{aligned}]-5[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 3\end{aligned}])\cdot [\begin{aligned}0 & 4\end{aligned}] \\  & =8([\begin{aligned}16 \\ -16\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}-10 \\ 15\end{aligned}])\cdot [\begin{aligned}0 & 4\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}208 \\ -248\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}0 & 4\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 832 \\ 0 & -992\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
